what_its_for: Dexchlorpheniramine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as runny nose, sneezing, itchy or watery eyes, and skin itching or rash. It can also help with symptoms of hay fever, hives, and reactions to insect stings or bites. It works by blocking histamine, the chemical your body releases during an allergic reaction.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with a small snack or glass of milk. Swallow extended-release tablets whole — do not crush, chew, or break them. Take it exactly as directed by your doctor or as shown on the label. Do not take more than the recommended amount.
dosing: For adults and children 12 years and older: The usual dose of regular tablets or liquid is 2 mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed, but no more than 12 mg in 24 hours. Extended-release tablets are usually taken as 4 mg to 6 mg every 8 to 10 hours. For children 6 to 11 years old: The usual dose is 1 mg every 4 to 6 hours, but no more than 6 mg in 24 hours. For children under 6 years old: Only use if your doctor tells you to, and follow their exact instructions. Always use the measuring cup or spoon that comes with liquid medicine — do not use a regular kitchen spoon.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and you are taking this medicine on a regular schedule, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your normal schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use this medicine after the expiration date on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can greatly increase drowsiness and dizziness. Avoid driving a car, operating heavy machinery, or doing any activity that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking other medicines that cause drowsiness, such as sleeping pills, anxiety medications, muscle relaxants, or other antihistamines, unless your doctor approves. Avoid taking other allergy or cold medicines at the same time without checking with your doctor or pharmacist, as many of them already contain antihistamines.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: difficulty urinating or are unable to urinate; fast, pounding, or irregular heartbeat; severe dizziness or confusion; vision changes or eye pain; seizures; or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing. Also contact your doctor if your symptoms do not improve after a few days or if they get worse.
when_it_works: Dexchlorpheniramine usually starts working within 15 to 30 minutes after you take a dose. Its effects typically last about 4 to 6 hours for regular tablets or liquid, and up to 8 to 10 hours for extended-release tablets. You should notice relief from sneezing, runny nose, and itching fairly quickly after your first dose.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): This medicine can cause more severe drowsiness, dizziness, and confusion in older people, which can increase the risk of falling. Use with extra caution and talk to your doctor about whether this is the right choice for you. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: This medicine may pass into breast milk and could harm a nursing baby. Talk to your doctor before using it if you are breastfeeding. Kidney or liver disease: Let your doctor know if you have kidney or liver problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Prostate problems or glaucoma: This medicine may make these conditions worse. Talk to your doctor before using it.
